This message comes from Schwab. At Schwab, you can get everything from self-directed investing to full-service wealth management, all in one place.
No matter your investing goal, life stage, amount to invest, or know-how, you can invest your way with Schwab.
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Lakshmi Singh.
It is not just President Trump who's barnstorming key states in the run-up to the midterm election.
Several high-profile Democratic Party figures are also on the campaign trail.
They include former President Barack Obama, who will be in Ohio and Michigan this weekend, then heads to Georgia next week.
And PR Stephen Fowler says Trump, meanwhile, has just announced he will hold a rally Monday in Mississippi, a state he won by more than 20 points in 2024.
It's really just the latest in deep red areas where polls show that the bottom could fall out for Republicans, like Kansas was before it, and even places like Iowa, Ohio, and Texas before that in this cycle.
The incumbent Sennihite Smith has performed worse than Trump in previous elections.
Cologne is a strong, moderate black candidate in a state that has the highest share of black voters in the country.
But it's also super racially polarized, meaning that white voters don't really vote for Democrats.
And PR Stephen Fowler reporting.
Russia and Ukraine exchange attacks overnight.
Local authorities in Ukraine say they leave at least nine people dead in Ukraine, with one person killed in Russia.
The fighting came despite a new push by the Trump administration to find an end to the conflict.
And PR Charles Maines has the latest from Moscow.
White House envoy Steve Whitcoff held talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin in St. Petersburg on Wednesday,
a meeting that saw Whitcoff praise the Kremlin leader as a humanitarian for releasing a wrongfully detained American.
And Putin agreed to rejoin U.S.-mediated talks with Ukraine.
Yet just hours later, Russia fired a barrage of missiles on Ukraine's capital Kiev, and Ukraine counter-withdrone attacks on Moscow.
Russia's defense ministry said it had targeted factories involved in the production of rockets and drones.
Yet Ukrainian President Vladimir Zelensky accused Russia of hitting civilian infrastructure, a sign he added that despite Whitcoff's praise for the Kremlin leader, Russia's position hadn't changed.
Charles Maines, NPR News, Moscow.
A new poll finds broad bipartisan support for tougher government regulation of artificial intelligence.
This from NPR's Windsor Johnston.
The survey by Navigator Research shows two-thirds of registered voters favor stronger government oversight of the A.I.
That includes nearly three-quarters of Democrats and more than six in ten Republicans.
And even among people who use A.I. frequently, 62 percent say they want more regulation.
The issue is also gaining attention as a priority in Washington.
Twenty-one percent of voters now rank A.I. among the top five issues the government should address.
That's three times as many as last December.
The poll also finds four in ten voters are more anxious than hopeful about A.I.
compared with just over a quarter who say they feel hopeful.
Windsor Johnston, NPR News, Washington.
You're listening to NPR News.
A federal judge is ordering President Trump to sit for a deposition in his $10 billion defamation lawsuit against the BBC and must do so by December 11th.
Trump had been scheduled for deposition last Friday, but his team canceled with little notice citing, quote, "matters of national importance."
The president accuses the publicly funded British broadcaster of editing a speech he delivered to supporters ahead of the insurrection on January 6, 2021
to make it seem as if he was directly calling for violence.
The BBC apologized for the edits.
Top executives resigned, but the BBC denies it defamed Trump.
A new analysis finds it now takes twice as long for Americans to save up for a start at home that it did seven years ago.
And P.S. Jennifer Ledin says a down payment and closing costs are big challenges.
Many renters might be able to afford a mortgage but don't have the cash to seal the deal.
And with rising rents and other costs, it's gotten a lot harder to save up for it, says Mike Calhoun,
is with the Julian Bond Institute at the Center for Responsible Lending.
For the median renter income, that requires 16 years of savings.
At that rate, the report notes, children may have moved out before a couple can move in to a first home.
The savings time needed is less for middle income and frontline workers like police officers and teachers 10 to 13 years.
But that's also twice as long as in 2019 before home prices and mortgage rates spiked.
Jennifer Ledin, NPR News, Washington.
Mortgage buyer Freddie Mike, meanwhile, says the average on a 30-year loan is 7.32 percent.
It's NPR News.
